newsitem.title: USA: Investors take 16 percent C-Phone stake. [CORRECTED 19:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Investors take 16 percent C-Phone stake. [CORRECTED 19:20 GMT]

text.p: Unidentified investors have taken a stake of about 16 percent in C-Phone Corp, a C-Phone spokesman said.
Shares of C-Phone, which makes picture telephones, rose 1-1/4 to 10.

C-Phone said the stake, which totals about $5 million, was taken for investment purposes and that Josephthal Lyons & Ross served as investment banker on the deal. The investors did not indicate if they would increase the stake.
(Corrects to clarify Josephthal Lyons & Ross not the 16 pct stakeholders).
Josephthal brought C-Phone public in August, 1994 at a price of $7.
The stake was taken incrementally during this past week as a private placement, the spokesman said.
Business Week first reported that an unidentified investor group has taken a 16 percent stake in the company.

C-Phone said on March 21 that the private electronics chain Nobody Beats the Wiz will begin marketing its system in time for the Mother's Day holiday. The chain has 60 stores in the New York metropolitan area.
The stock went from 6-3/4 on March 20 to 11-3/8 the next day, when C-Phone announced the Wiz deal. The stock had traded between $2 and $4 much of last year, then shot as high as $19 in January.
